The control of insulin secretion 
Potent metabolic stimuli to insulin secretion are glucose and some amino acids that act synergistically.   

Gastrointestinal hormones (incretin effect) glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP).

Autonomic nerves innervate islets. May account for a small increase in insulin secretion that may occur before the entry of food into the gastrointestinal tract.

slides.text:
Key metabolic role of the liver in glucose metabolism
Coverts galactose and fructose to glucose
Stores glucose as glycogen, when blood glucose is high
Glycogenolysis to release glucose into blood
Gluconeogenesis: converts amino acids and glycerol to glucose when glycogen levels drop
De-novo lipogenesis – converts glucose to fat for storage

slides.text:
Type 2 diabetes
Beta cells of the pancreas initially produce insulin but the body is unable to use it effectively because the cells of the body are resistant to the action of insulin. 
Diabetes is not simply a disease of high blood glucose, but a disease of impaired coordination between the major fuel stores and fuel-consuming tissues of the body.

Accounts for 90% of all diabetic individuals
- Complications include 
atherosclerosis, neurological changes, renal failure and blindness
In type 2 diabetes, insulin resistance disrupts whole-body fuel partitioning, so glucose is not effectively cleared by muscle while the liver continues to release glucose, causing a mismatch between substrate supply and utilization

slides.topic: Whole-body Glucose Metabolism — Insulin, Glucagon & Resistance — source 18
slides.text:
What is insulin resistance?
Insulin resistance is often defined based on measurements
of glucose metabolism
The ability of insulin to reduce blood glucose is impaired (clearance) in blood
The ability of insulin to reduce glucose production.
	(production rate) in blood
Insulin also regulates the anabolism and storage of fat, protein synthesis, and non-metabolic process such as cell growth and differentiation. 

It is important to note that not all insulin-dependent processes and tissues are
equally resistant to insulin.

slides.topic: Whole-body Glucose Metabolism — Insulin, Glucagon & Resistance — source 26
slides.text:
Management of Type 2 diabetes 
First line of treatment: diet and exercise (lose weight). Improves insulin resistance and lowers blood glucose levels.

Unfortunately, despite best efforts, many cannot lose weight or cannot maintain their weight loss, or their blood glucose levels are poorly controlled despite weight loss. 

Only alternative is drug/insulin treatment.

Majority will go onto insulin therapy
